page: Microsoft Azure D48s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 series, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The system exposes 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 192.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor is equipped with 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 instruction sets.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput across compute, cryptographic, and memory-bound operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,375.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 63,181.51, with PassMark encryption operations measuring 50,074.91. Memory subsystem tests report uncached large-block read bandwidth of 253.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 104.76 GB/sec. CPU matrix capabilities show in machine learning inference evaluations, where the instance processed 349.67 tokens per second during generation with a 135M model and 32.09 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The hardware configuration includes zero bundled local storage drives and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached Azure Premium Storage for operating system and data volumes. Network and cache throughput support high operational density, verified by 66.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 81.09 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Workload fit centers on enterprise application hosting, large-scale CI/CD build environments, in-memory caching tiers, and CPU-based model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D48s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores using an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 192.0 GB of memory and a 260 MB L3 cache, the platform delivers a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The CPU incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, driving strong synthetic and real-world processing metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 63,181.51 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 20,375.0. Memory bandwidth remains high with uncached read throughput exceeding 253 GB/sec. Operating without local storage, the instance relies on Azure Premium Storage for persistent data. Its performance profile fits high-concurrency web tiers, Redis in-memory databases, continuous integration build jobs, and CPU-bound model inference.
